around.headline: Poll survey team assaulted in Bengaluru's DJ Halli during electoral roll revision
around.summary: An official conducting the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was assaulted in DJ Halli; two people have been arrested. If a Booth Level Officer visits your home for this exercise, ask to see their ID card and authorization letter before sharing any documents.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Conflicting word on Bengaluru's water supply: 15-hour cut planned for July 31, but BWSSB denies a shortage
around.summary: One report says parts of Bengaluru face a 15-hour water supply disruption on July 31, while BWSSB and other outlets insist there's no city-wide shortage — though a separate report notes reservoir stock is enough for only about 4 more months. If you're in an affected area, store a day's worth of water tomorrow just in case.
around.source: The News Minute, The New Indian Express, Times of India

around.headline: Minor fire breaks out at Nagasandra Metro Station
around.summary: A small fire was reported at Nagasandra Metro Station on the Green Line. Commuters on that stretch should check for delays before heading out this evening.

around.headline: Bengaluru hotels warn of Swiggy, Zomato boycott from August 15 over payment disputes
around.summary: Restaurants across the city say they'll stop taking orders from Swiggy and Zomato from August 15 over unauthorised deductions and payment disputes, giving the platforms 15 days to fix it. If this holds, expect fewer restaurant options on food delivery apps from mid-August.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Times of India

around.headline: Traffic police seek higher penalties after 50% discount scheme on fines backfires
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police are pushing for steeper penalties after a scheme offering 50% discounts on old challans failed to deter repeat violations. Expect fines to get costlier if you're still sitting on unpaid challans or tend to bend traffic rules.

around.headline: Trump says Russia sanctions bill threatening 100% tariffs on India isn't 'necessary,' but it's still moving
around.summary: US President Trump commented on a Congressional sanctions bill that could impose 100% tariffs on India over its Russian oil purchases, calling it not strictly necessary without ruling it out. A tariff of that scale could ripple into prices of imported goods and India's export-driven sectors if it goes through.

street_smart.title: A person shows up at your door saying they're a Booth Level Officer doing the government's door-to-door voter roll revision (SIR), and asks for your Aadhaar number, family details, and a photo of your ID card right now. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's news that a survey team conducting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was assaulted in Bengaluru's DJ Halli — a reminder that this door-to-door exercise is actively underway across the city right now, which also makes it an easy cover for impersonators.
street_smart.situation: Bengaluru's electoral roll revision is underway, and officials really are visiting homes to update voter records — but that same cover makes it easy for a scammer to show up asking for more than they should.

choices.text: Ask to see the BLO's printed ID card and the Election Commission's authorization letter, note down their name and ID number, and only share the details already on your existing voter ID/EPIC — no OTPs, no Aadhaar copies, no bank details.
choices.feedback: Correct. Genuine BLOs always carry a printed ID and an authorization letter, and the SIR exercise only needs your existing voter roll details, not OTPs or financial information. Noting their name and ID number gives you something to follow up on if anything about the visit seems off.

choices.text: Hand over a photocopy of your Aadhaar card and let them note your mobile number and bank details 'for verification,' since they're wearing a government-looking jacket.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A jacket or lanyard proves nothing — genuine electoral roll revision never requires Aadhaar copies, bank details, or your mobile number for 'verification.' Handing these over gives an impersonator everything needed for identity theft or a follow-up OTP scam, while a real BLO would never ask for them in the first place.

choices.text: Refuse to open the door or answer any questions at all, and tell them to come back another time.
choices.feedback: Blanket refusal isn't safe either — if this is a genuine BLO, dodging the visit can get your name flagged or dropped from the voter roll during the revision. Verify credentials first, then cooperate with the legitimate parts of the process instead of stonewalling.

choices.text: Answer their questions and share your basic details verbally, without asking for ID or writing down who visited.
choices.feedback: Even a low-risk conversation should leave a paper trail. Without recording the visitor's name and ID number, you have no way to confirm later whether the visit was genuine or to report it if something about your voter record changes unexpectedly.

takeaways: Genuine Booth Level Officers carry a printed ID card and an Election Commission authorization letter — always ask to see both before sharing anything.
The SIR/voter roll exercise never needs your Aadhaar OTP, bank details, or a photocopy of your Aadhaar — only your existing voter ID/EPIC information.
You can check or update your own voter roll entry anytime via the CEO Karnataka website or the Voter Helpline app/1950, without waiting for a doorstep visit.

quiz.q: Bengaluru hotels have warned they'll stop taking orders from which food delivery platforms starting August 15, over payment disputes?
quiz.why: The hotels' associations say unauthorised deductions and unresolved payment disputes with the platforms prompted the 15-day ultimatum.

quiz.q: A minor fire was reported today at which Bengaluru metro station on the Green Line?
quiz.why: Nagasandra is one of the northern terminus stations of the Green Line, serving commuters heading toward Tumkur Road.

quiz.q: A recent report says Bengaluru's reservoir water stock is currently enough to last for only about how many more months?
quiz.why: The estimate has stirred debate since separate civic officials maintain there's no immediate city-wide shortage.

quiz.q: Which body is constitutionally responsible for conducting exercises like the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls?
quiz.why: The Election Commission derives this authority from Article 324 of the Constitution, which makes it independent of the government of the day.

quiz.q: The KRS Dam, a key reservoir feeding Bengaluru's water supply, is built across which river?
quiz.why: The Krishna Raja Sagar dam near Mysuru is one of the major reservoirs on the Cauvery, which also flows through Tamil Nadu downstream.
